findings.summary: Occasional builders were the largest group (11 of 30), followed by browsers who rarely buy (9); regular builders numbered 6 and gift/souvenir buyers 4.
The most common expected price was $40-$59 (13 of 30, 43.3%), with $20-$39 (8) and $60-$99 (7) next; no one chose 'Not sure'.
Nearly half (14 of 30, 46.7%) would pay up to 10% more in person, while 7 expect the same or lower price; only 2 would pay more than 25% more.
Half (15 of 30) expect to buy 1 kit per year, 7 expect 0 and 7 expect 2-3; only 1 expects 4-6 and none 7 or more.
Price and value relative to online dominated (27 of 30, 90.0%), followed by exclusivity/limited editions (20), knowledgeable staff (18) and kit quality (18); souvenir appeal was mentioned by only 8.
quotes: Price is the biggest factor, plain and simple. I'd look at the kit quality, detail, and whether they have something I can't easily get online, but I'm not paying a big Times Square markup just because of the address. A sale or fair price would matter more than fancy display or location.
I'd also pay more if the staff can speak knowledgeably about materials, build difficulty, and what's worth buying, but I'm not drawn to artificial scarcity or hype pricing.

I'd spend more if the kit looked well designed, had good instructions, and felt worth displaying or learning from rather than being just a trendy souvenir. Price would also depend on the subject, the quality of the molding, and whether the store staff could answer detailed questions honestly.

caveats: Respondents are AI personas generated by Flashpoint's synthetic panel, not real people. Treat these results as directional.
Sample size of 30 is small, so single-response options (e.g., $100 or more, 4-6 kits) are very unstable.
All responses were collected on a single day (14 November 2026), so no variation over time is captured.
Q5 themes were coded by Flashpoint's analysis and responses can fall into multiple themes, so theme counts do not sum to 30.
Stated prices and purchase frequency are not observed spending; rent, wholesale costs, competition and the legality of selling knockoffs were not studied.
